words.gloss: body; only; from seeing: from merely seeing the body
large; body; -ness: from largeness of body

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, वैद्य केवल देह को देखने मात्र से भ्रमित न हो कि 'यह उपचय यानी शरीर की पुष्टि से या बड़े शरीर के कारण बलवान है, और यह दुबलेपन से या छोटे शरीर के कारण अल्प बल वाला है।'
english: On a conjectural reading, a physician should not be deluded merely by seeing the body alone, thinking: 'This one is strong because of bulk (upacaya) or because of a large body; this one is of little strength because of thinness or because of a small body.'

text_flags.why: possible: 'mucyet' (should be released) gives no sense after 'na ... bhiṣak'; 'muhyet' (should be deluded) fits the quoted wrong inferences that follow; cy/hy confusion in the scan

notes: The printed 'mucyed' (mucyet, 'should be released') gives no sense here; 'muhyed' ('should be deluded', ca/ha confusion) fits the sense and is adopted on a conjectural reading, so the translations carry the mark. 'bhiṣag' is the subject; the two 'ayam' are the two cases quoted ('this one ... this one ...'). Printed 'balaiti' is 'bala iti' written together (hiatus). Printed 'rddh/-tt' style doubling is not involved here. upacaya = accumulation, plumpness of flesh (standard).

words.gloss: elephant; lion: in the elephant and the lion

hindi: और वे दोनों भी हाथी और सिंह में अन्य प्रकार से देखे गए हैं।
english: And both of these are also seen to be otherwise in the elephant and the lion.
notes: Refers back to the two inferences quoted in 75 (strong from a large body; weak from a small body). 'gajasiṃhe' is read as a locative of the dvandva 'gaja-siṃha' (elephant and lion); the text does not say in which way each is 'otherwise'. 'api' is rendered 'also'.

words.gloss: supreme; heaviness, weight, gravity; joined with
with resonance; smooth; deep; great; voice

hindi: वहाँ सब सारों से युक्त होने वाला अत्यन्त बलवान, अत्यन्त गौरव यानी भारीपन से युक्त, क्लेश सहने में समर्थ, सब आरम्भों में अपने में आशा रखने वाला, कल्याण में लगनशील, स्थिर शरीर वाला, सुसंयत गति वाला, अनुनाद सहित स्निग्ध गम्भीर और महान् स्वर वाला, सुख, ऐश्वर्य और धन के उपभोग वाला, सम्मान पाने वाला, मन्द जरा और मन्द रोग वाला, प्रायः समान गुणों वाली विस्तृत सन्तान वाला और दीर्घायु होता है।
english: There, one endowed with all the essences (sāra) is exceedingly strong, endowed with great heaviness (gaurava), able to bear hardship, having hope in himself in all undertakings, devoted to the good, steady in body, of well-composed gait, with a resonant, smooth, deep and great voice, with the enjoyment of comfort, lordship and wealth, receiving honour, with slow old age and mild illness, usually with widely extended offspring of equal qualities, and long-lived.
notes: The sāras themselves are not listed in this unit; 'sāra' is rendered 'essence'. 'tatra' (there, among these) has no stated antecedent. 'gaurava' is bodily heaviness or gravity of bearing (dignity is an alternative sense). 'manda' is taken with both jarā and āmaya (slow/mild); 'prāyaḥ' (usually) could be taken with the preceding or the following phrase. 'vistīrṇa-apatya' = offspring that are extensive/numerous. 'sānunāda' = with resonance (anunāda). All adjectives qualify the one endowed with all sāras (subject understood from 'upaitaḥ').

hindi: उसका विपरीत तो असार यानी सार से रहित है; मध्य वाला मध्यम गुणों वाला है।
english: The opposite of that, however, is without essence (asāra); the middle one has middling qualities.
notes: 'tat' is taken as the one endowed with all sāras (77). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed. Whether 'asāra' means entirely lacking every sāra is not stated.

hindi: प्रमाण फिर अपने अंगुलों यानी अंगुल की चौड़ाई से है।
english: The measure, moreover, is by one's own aṅgulas (finger-breadths).
notes: Introduces the measurements that follow. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

words.gloss: of the foot; big toe; second toe (pradeśinī, lit. pointing one)

hindi: पैर के अँगूठे और प्रदेशिनी यानी अँगूठे के बाद की अंगुली दो अंगुल लम्बी हैं; अन्य तीन क्रम से आगे-आगे पाँचवें भाग से हीन हैं, या उनके नख से हीन हैं।
english: The big toe and the second toe (pradeśinī) of the foot are two aṅgulas long; the other three, in order, each successive one, are less by a fifth part, or less by their nail.
notes: Final -hīnā before 'vā' is regular sandhi (hīnāḥ vā). 'tat-nakha' = the nail of those (toes); the text does not say how a nail's length is fixed. pradeśinī (index finger) applied to the foot = second toe (standard). 'Other three' are the remaining toes, not named. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

words.gloss: front of the foot (prapada); sole (pādatala); heel (pāṣṇi)

hindi: प्रपद, पादतल और पाष्णि अलग-अलग चार अंगुल लम्बे हैं, और छः, पाँच और चार अंगुल चौड़े हैं; पैर लम्बाई में चौदह ही है और घेरे में चौदह ही है।
english: The prapada (front of the foot), the sole (pādatala) and the heel (pāṣṇi) are separately four aṅgulas long, and are spread six, five and four aṅgulas broad; the foot is exactly fourteen in length and exactly fourteen in girth.
notes: Pairing of the widths six, five, four with the three parts follows their order (natural reading, not stated). The three lengths of four plus the two of the big toe (80) make fourteen, which agrees with the foot's length; this is an observation only. 'aṅgula' is understood after the numerals. prapada = forepart of the foot, pāṣṇi = heel (standard). Final -āḥ/-aḥ before c is regular sandhi (vistṛtāś, pādaś). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: वैसे ही दोनों गुल्फ यानी टखने और जंघा यानी घुटने से नीचे की पिंडली का मध्य।
english: Likewise the two ankles (gulpha) and the middle of the shank (jaṅghā).
notes: Elliptical: no measure and no verb are printed here; both are carried from the neighbouring units, but the text does not say which measure. Unit 83 begins a new item (the foot's height). gulpha = ankle (standard); jaṅghā = the lower leg between knee and ankle (standard); in Hindi jaṅghā is not the thigh.

hindi: पैर ऊँचाई में चार अंगुल का है।
english: The foot is four aṅgulas in height.
notes: Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: जंघा यानी घुटने से नीचे की पिंडली और ऊरु यानी जाँघ लम्बाई में अठारह हैं।
english: The shank (jaṅghā) and the thigh (ūru) are eighteen in length.
notes: 'aṣṭādaśāyāmā' is feminine singular, agreeing with jaṅghā, and is understood for both. ūru = thigh (standard). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: जानु यानी घुटना चार अंगुल का है।
english: The knee (jānu) is of four aṅgulas.
notes: The dimension (length, breadth) is not stated. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: ऊरु यानी जाँघ घेरे में तीस अंगुल की है।
english: The thigh is thirty aṅgulas in girth.
notes: Printed 'pariṇāhaūruḥ' = pariṇāhaḥ + ūruḥ (visarga lost in hiatus, regular). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: मुष्क यानी अण्डकोश और मेढ्र यानी शिश्न, दोनों लम्बाई में छः हैं और घेरे में आठ और पाँच हैं।
english: The muṣka (scrotum or testicles) and the meḍhra (penis) are both six in length, and eight and five in girth.
notes: Printed 'meṃḍhra' is read meḍhra (nasal before the conjunct; spelling normalised). Pairing 'eight and five' with the two organs in order is the natural reading, not stated. muṣka = testicle/scrotum (standard, the dictionaries give both), meḍhra = penis (standard). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: कटी यानी कमर का भाग चौड़ाई में सोलह और घेरे में पचास है।
english: The kaṭī (hip or waist region) is sixteen in breadth and fifty in girth.
notes: kaṭī = hip/waist region (standard). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

words.gloss: bladder; head: head of the bladder

hindi: बस्तिशिर यानी मूत्राशय का शिर दस अंगुल का है।
english: The basti-śiras ('head of the bladder'; basti = bladder) is ten aṅgulas.
notes: basti = urinary bladder (standard); 'basti-śiras' is kept literal, and the exact part meant (the top of the bladder, or the region above it) is not stated here. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: उदर यानी पेट बारह अंगुल का है।
english: The belly (udara) is twelve aṅgulas.
notes: Here udara is the belly (body part), not a disease. The dimension is not stated. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: पार्श्व यानी दोनों बगलें चौड़ाई में दस और लम्बाई में बारह हैं।
english: The two flanks (pārśva) are ten in breadth and twelve in length.
notes: 'vistāre' and 'āyāme' may be locatives ('in breadth', 'in length') or dual forms agreeing with 'pārśve'; the sense is the same. pārśva = flank, side of the trunk (standard). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

words.gloss: trika (probably the sacral region of the lower back)

hindi: त्रिक यानी सम्भवतः पीठ के निचले भाग का त्रिकास्थि वाला स्थान ऊँचाई में बारह है।
english: The trika (probably the sacral region of the lower back) is twelve in height.
notes: trika = the lower back where the spine meets the pelvis, sacrum (probable). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: पृष्ठ यानी पीठ ऊँचाई में अठारह है।
english: The back (pṛṣṭha) is eighteen in height.
notes: Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: स्तनान्तर यानी दोनों स्तनों के बीच का अन्तर बारह का है।
english: The interval between the breasts (stanāntara) is a set of twelve.
notes: 'dvādaśaka' = a group of twelve. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: स्तन का पर्यन्त यानी छोर दो अंगुल का है।
english: The limit (paryanta) of the breast is two aṅgulas.
notes: 'paryanta' = boundary, extremity; it may mean the breast's own extent or the edge region; the text does not say. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: उरस् यानी छाती चौबीस अंगुल चौड़ी और ऊँचाई में बारह है।
english: The chest (uras) is twenty-four aṅgulas broad and twelve in height.
notes: Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: हृदय यानी दिल दो अंगुल का है।
english: The heart (hṛdaya) is of two aṅgulas.
notes: hṛdaya = heart (standard). The dimension is not stated. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

words.gloss: of eight, a set of eight

hindi: दोनों स्कन्ध आठ के हैं, और दोनों कक्ष यानी काँख भी।
english: The two shoulders (skandha) are of eight, and the two armpits too.
notes: 'aṣṭakau' is masculine dual and agrees only with 'skandhau'; that the armpits share the measure is understood from 'ca'. kakṣa = armpit (standard). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

words.gloss: of six, a set of six (conjectured; printed ṣaḍḍā)

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, दोनों अंस यानी सम्भवतः कन्धे के जोड़ छः के हैं।
english: On a conjectural reading, the two aṃsa (probably the shoulder-joints) are of six.

text_flags.why: possible: 'ṣaḍḍā' is not a form; the parallel dual numerals in 98, 100, 101 (aṣṭakau, ṣoḍaśakau, pañcadaśakau) suggest 'ṣaṭkau aṃsau' = ṣaṭkāv aṃsau (ṭk/ḍḍ confusion in the scan); conjectural

notes: Printed 'ṣaḍḍāvaṃsau' is not a regular form. The neighbouring units 98, 100, 101 use dual '-ka' forms (aṣṭakau, ṣoḍaśakau, pañcadaśakau); 'ṣaṭkau' + 'aṃsau' would give 'ṣaṭkāvaṃsau', close to the print, so this is a possible reading only. The numeral 'six' and 'aṃsa' are fairly sure; the middle syllables are not. aṃsa (shoulder or shoulder-joint) is probable; skandha in 98 is also rendered shoulder, and how the two differ is not stated here. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

words.gloss: of sixteen, a set of sixteen
two prabāhu (an arm segment, identity disputed)

hindi: दोनों प्रबाहु यानी भुजा का एक भाग, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, सोलह के हैं।
english: The two prabāhu (a segment of the arm; identity disputed) are of sixteen.
notes: prabāhu is given as 'forearm' in some dictionaries and as part of the upper limb in others; identity disputed, so the Sanskrit term is kept. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

words.gloss: of fifteen, a set of fifteen
two prapāṇi (a part of the hand or arm, identity disputed)

hindi: दोनों प्रपाणि यानी हाथ या बाँह का एक भाग, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, पन्द्रह के हैं।
english: The two prapāṇi (a part of the hand or arm; identity disputed) are of fifteen.
notes: prapāṇi is unclear: a length of fifteen is longer than the hand (twelve, 102), so a part of the arm is possible, but this is not certain; identity disputed, Sanskrit term kept. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: दोनों हाथ बारह अंगुल के हैं; उनमें भी मध्यमा अंगुली पाँच अंगुल की है।
english: The two hands (pāṇi) are twelve aṅgulas; in them as well, the middle finger is five aṅgulas.
notes: Printed 'paṃcāṃgulāmadhyamāṃguliḥ' = pañcāṅgulā madhyamāṅguliḥ. 'tatra api' could also be 'even there (in each hand)'. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: उससे आधा अंगुल हीन प्रदेशिनी यानी तर्जनी और अनामिका हैं।
english: Less than that by half an aṅgula are the index finger (pradeśinī) and the ring finger (anāmikā).
notes: Printed 'arddha' = ardha (doubling after r, print habit; normalised). 'tataḥ' refers to the five aṅgulas of the middle finger (102). anāmikā ('nameless') = ring finger (standard). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: कनिष्ठिका यानी छोटी अंगुली और अँगूठा साढ़े तीन अंगुल के हैं।
english: The little finger (kaniṣṭhikā) and the thumb (aṅguṣṭha) are three and a half aṅgulas.
notes: Printed 'sārddha' = sārdha (doubling after r; normalised). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: शिरोधरा यानी गर्दन ऊँचाई में चार और घेरे में बाईस है।
english: The neck (śirodharā) is four in height and twenty-two in girth.
notes: śirodharā = neck (standard). Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: आनन यानी चेहरा ऊँचाई में बारह और घेरे में चौबीस है।
english: The face (ānana) is twelve in height and twenty-four in girth.
notes: ānana = face; āsya in 107 = mouth. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

hindi: आस्य यानी मुँह पाँच अंगुल का है।
english: The mouth (āsya) is of five aṅgulas.
notes: The dimension (opening, width) is not stated. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

words.gloss: chin; lip; nose; interval of the eyes; ear; forehead

hindi: चिबुक यानी ठुड्डी, ओष्ठ यानी होंठ, नासा यानी नाक, दृष्टि-अन्तर यानी सम्भवतः आँखों के बीच की दूरी, कर्ण यानी कान और ललाट यानी माथा, अलग-अलग चार अंगुल के हैं।
english: Separately, four aṅgulas: the chin (cibuka), the lip (oṣṭha), the nose (nāsā), the interval between the eyes (dṛṣṭy-antara, probably), the ear (karṇa) and the forehead (lalāṭa).

text_flags.why: possible: doubled d in 'nāsāddṛṣṭy-' is not required inside a compound; may be a spurious doubling, or nāsāt + dṛṣṭyantara (which would change the sense)

notes: Printed 'nāsāddṛṣṭy-' has a doubled d: either a spurious doubling (flagged) or 'nāsāt dṛṣṭy-antara'. 'dṛṣṭy-antara' is read as the interval between the eyes (probable); 'nāsā-dṛṣṭy-antara' as one item, the nose-to-eye interval, is a possible alternative. The compound is a neuter singular dvandva (caturaṅgulam). cibuka, oṣṭha, karṇa, lalāṭa are standard. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

words.gloss: a third part of an aṅgula in breadth

hindi: नासापुट यानी नथुने की मर्यादा यानी किनारा चौड़ाई में अंगुल का तिहाई भाग है।
english: The border (maryādā) of the nostril (nāsāpuṭa) is a third part of an aṅgula in breadth.
notes: 'tribhāga' is taken as a third part; 'three parts' of an aṅgula is an alternative. maryādā = border, limit. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

words.gloss: thumb; belly; spread: broad by the belly of the thumb

hindi: नेत्र यानी आँख दो अंगुल लम्बी है और अँगूठे के उदर यानी पेट की चौड़ाई वाली है।
english: The eye (netra) is two aṅgulas long and broad by the belly (udara) of the thumb.
notes: 'aṅguṣṭhodara' = the belly, i.e. the fleshy middle of the thumb; the text gives no further measure, so it is not enriched. Here udara is a body part, not a disease. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.

words.gloss: sight, the seeing part (probably the pupil)

hindi: उसमें कृष्ण यानी काला भाग शुक्ल यानी सफेद भाग का तीसरा अंश है; कृष्ण का नौवाँ अंश, मसूर यानी मसूर दाल के दल जितना, दृष्टि है, सम्भवतः पुतली।
english: In it, the black (part) is a third portion of the white; the dṛṣṭi (the seeing part, probably the pupil) is a ninth portion of the black, of the size of a masūra-dala (half of a lentil, or a lentil leaf).
notes: Read as 'the black is a third portion of the white' (śuklasya tṛtīyāṃśaḥ); 'tṛtīya-aṃśa' = one third or the third portion. 'dṛṣṭi' = the seeing part, probably the pupil. masūra = lentil, Lens culinaris (standard); 'dala' = half-seed, split, or leaf (ambiguous). Final -ā of 'navamāṃśā' agrees with feminine dṛṣṭi. Copula 'is/are' supplied (copula understood); the unit of measure (aṅgula) is understood where only a numeral is printed.
